lead: A member answering `CoreTy::Instance(C)` panics at run time while `C` has no instance member and no slot
body: , because `crates/nvs-stdlib/src/instance.rs:270` skips such a class when it builds the descriptor table, so the call compiles and type-checks and then dies in `FATAL: … is not a `Core` class with instances`. It reads like a registry wiring mistake and is an ordering fact. Land the class's first instance member in the slice that first answers one — the conformance floor wants it too, a handle with no members having no three questions to be asked.
